Three centroids of a reliability profile

Source: R/algebra-centroids.R
reliability_centroids.Rd

Computes the harmonic centroid, the informativeness and the mean reliability of a set of site reliabilities.

Usage

reliability_centroids(S)

Arguments

S

Site reliabilities, a numeric vector of numbers strictly between 0 and 1, as returned by site_reliability().

Value

A named numeric vector with elements harmonic, I (the informativeness) and mean.

Details

The three numbers are the first-argument centroids of the reliabilities under three Bregman divergences (Lee, 2026, Table 2): the harmonic mean (Burg potential), the informativeness \(I\) (Bernoulli Kullback-Leibler) and the arithmetic mean \(\bar S\) (squared error). The harmonic centroid is never larger than the other two, and equals them only when all the reliabilities are equal. There is no general order between \(I\) and the mean reliability: either can be the larger, depending on the level and the skewness of the profile, and the sign of their difference is reported by local_terms().

References

Lee, J. (2026). The geometry of informativeness: A Bregman-centroid diagnostic for partial pooling in multisite trials. Unpublished manuscript.

See also

bregman_centroid() for the centroids on either side of each divergence.

Examples

S <- site_reliability(se = c(0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.30), sigma_tau = 0.2)
reliability_centroids(S)
#>  harmonic         I      mean 
#> 0.4961240 0.5714286 0.5619231
